scenario: A time-constrained independent recruiter captures one authorized Signal, binds the exact Person and Pursuit, reviews evidence and a revision-checked Proposal, applies once, records an owned internal action outcome, and recovers exact canonical receipts across interruption, response loss, stale authority, relaunch, and deletion without external effects.

review_plan.reason: The artifact must close a useful, low-burden recruiter momentum loop across ordinary and recovery states.
Identity, evidence authority, deletion, idempotency, stale state, and response loss are release-critical.
The shipping surface must remain truthful, reachable, calm, and accessible on the smallest supported phone.
Consent, identity, uncertainty, and timely human follow-through affect candidate dignity and trust.
The artifact does not assess, score, rank, infer fit, or predict a candidate.

findings.observation: The frozen local artifact closes the recruiter-controlled loop, but it does not compare completion time, correction burden, or stale-action rate against the recruiter's manual note, ATS, message, and calendar fallback.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-04 artifact.json explicitly lists design-partner recruiter field comparison and authorized candidate-side research as known missing proof; the executable bundle is synthetic-only.
findings.user_impact: Release can be judged operationally safe and coherent in the frozen local scope, but claims that it is faster or more useful than a practiced manual workflow would remain unearned.
findings.recommendation: Keep field-efficiency claims out of release language and run a design-partner comparison on the exact capture-to-recovery loop.
findings.verification: Representative independent recruiters complete seeded normal, ambiguity, interruption, response-loss, and no-action cases in Talent Signal and their normal fallback; report time, corrections, context switches, duplicate work, and stale-action rate without candidate scoring.

strengths: Frozen-object verification passed before review: 195/195 source hashes, 39/39 evidence hashes, 21/21 screenshot hashes, source aggregate 76f34380d01a02ebe9f2d6f7a21f0d639aea7772a25e8a3e0a2a08f90aa6dabb, and repository commit 2c19567f2d3b0e8e6a986fb8b420f4ac5b9c7435 all match TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-04.

Restored evidence-review authority fails closed: RelationshipArchiveTests/testSupersededPersistenceFailureKeepsSessionTerminalGuard proves a failed superseded save remains readback-locked after relaunch, and the exact/newer readback tests prove only matching availability, review status, and authority review ID unlock while newer authority becomes terminal. RelationshipAskView exposes only Check current evidence in the locked state, and revalidation is called only after an explicit successful Ask.

Owned-action response loss is calm and recoverable: CandidateSignalUITests/testOwnedActionResponseLossRelaunchReconcilesWithoutSecondPost verifies one POST, one canonical receipt, removal of the duplicate Today attention row, revision 2 readback, no Waiting for review label, and no stale Proposal affordance. The locked, Today recovery, and reconciled screenshots make that transition inspectable.

Canonical state does not leave obsolete work open: pursuit-domain-runtime.json reports action_revision_supersedes_open_proposal=pass, while the backend marks older needs_review Proposals and pending items superseded in the same action-completion transaction and records an audit event.

Identity, deletion, and response-loss paths remain recruiter-legible: the same-name receipt preserves distinct Person/role/context IDs; the deletion receipt states server confirmation precedes local payload removal; Proposal and action unknown-outcome screens lock resubmission until canonical readback.

All 71 P0 assertions and 12 file proofs resolve to 23 unique dependencies under the Retest 04 evidence root, and every dependency is present in the 39-entry artifact evidence manifest; no transitive P0 reference escapes the frozen artifact.

reviews.lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: The protected action-operation chain reconciles safely, but Today exposes only the newest saved action recovery. If two different Pursuits have response-lost action operations, the older operation can lose its Today recovery entry after its canonical action no longer produces ordinary attention.
findings.evidence: Direct source evidence at frozen commit 2c19567f2d3b0e8e6a986fb8b420f4ac5b9c7435: apps/ios/Sources/Features/PursuitWorkspaceStore.swift, latestActionRecovery(in:), sorts saved entries and returns from the first matching entry; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift, PursuitTodayView, accepts one PursuitActionRecoveryItem? and deduplicates only that Pursuit. The frozen ios-full-suite-runtime.json check owned_action_response_loss_reconciles_without_second_post covers one recovery Pursuit, and action-response-loss-today-recovery.png directly shows that single recovery card.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter managing several searches may not notice an older unresolved or recently reconciled owned outcome from Today. The operation remains locked and does not duplicate or claim false success, so this is a bounded discoverability gap rather than an authorization veto.
findings.recommendation: Project every protected action recovery, grouped once per Pursuit, with a compact disclosure when several exist; continue suppressing the ordinary attention row only for the exact Pursuit represented by each recovery item.
findings.verification: Create response loss for owned actions in two different Pursuits, relaunch, and prove both recovery entries are reachable from Today, neither Pursuit is duplicated as ordinary attention, each canonical readback binds its own operation/receipt, and each action-completion POST count increases by exactly one.

findings.observation: Action completion canonically supersedes an older Proposal only when its status is needs_review, while the open Proposal API also returns confirming, conflict, and failed statuses. An older conflict or failed Proposal can therefore remain in the canonical open queue after the Pursuit advances, although iOS defensively prevents review when the base revision is stale.
findings.evidence: Direct source evidence at frozen commit 2c19567f2d3b0e8e6a986fb8b420f4ac5b9c7435: apps/backend/src/modules/pursuits.ts, completePursuitAction(), updates pursuit_proposals only where status = 'needs_review' and base_revision is older; apps/backend/src/modules/pursuitProposals.ts, listPursuitProposals(), includes needs_review, confirming, conflict, and failed. Supported inference: an old conflict/failed row remains API-visible because the frozen runPursuitDomainEvaluation.ts and pursuit-domain-runtime.json assertion action_revision_supersedes_open_proposal exercise only a freshly staged needs_review Proposal. apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift filters exact current base revisions and labels stale rows non-authoritative, bounding the immediate iOS harm.
findings.user_impact: A future client or queue consumer that trusts the canonical open-Proposal list can surface obsolete work after a revision change. The current iOS does not allow that stale Proposal to execute, so no active false-success or unauthorized-mutation veto is present.
findings.recommendation: Define the canonical nonterminal/open status set once and supersede every older member when an independent Pursuit mutation advances revision; preserve the prior status and cause in append-only audit metadata.
findings.verification: Stage a Proposal, force it into conflict (and failed if that status is supported), then complete an owned action at the current revision; assert the Proposal becomes superseded, pending items become epistemically superseded, it disappears from listPursuitProposals(), the supersession audit names owned_action_outcome, and stale review remains rejected.

findings.observation: The frozen P0 runtime reports 71 assertions, but P0-08 repeats the same pending-inbox and background-interruption assertions twice, leaving 69 unique assertion objects.
findings.evidence: Direct inspection of the hash-verified evidence/p0-journey-manifest.json shows checks.pending_inbox_restores_reviewed_draft twice and checks.background_interruption_preserves_review_decision twice under P0-08; evidence/p0-journey-runtime.json reports assertion_count 71. All 23 unique assertion/file dependencies are still present under the frozen evidence root and included in artifact.json, so dependency integrity itself passes.
findings.user_impact: The numerical assertion count slightly overstates independent coverage and can make later evaluator comparisons less trustworthy, without changing any product safety result.
findings.recommendation: Deduplicate journey assertions by source, path, and expectation during manifest generation and fail validation when an exact duplicate is present.
findings.verification: Regenerate the frozen manifest; P0-08 contains each check once, the validator reports only unique assertions, and all dependency paths remain inside and hashed by the frozen evidence manifest.

strengths: The frozen authority path fails closed across persistence failure and process relaunch: restored pending/outcome-unknown/failed evidence reviews are readback-locked, cannot be claimed, and cannot POST until a successful explicit Ask returns exact current canonical citation authority; a newer authority terminally supersedes the old operation.

Backend evidence-review authority is append-only and revision-bound: same-cycle idempotent replay returns the same review, later review authority rejects the old replay with EVIDENCE_REVIEW_AUTHORITY_STALE, and the frozen runtime verifies the three-link persisted chain.

Owned action and Proposal response-loss paths withhold success, persist one recovery identity, reconcile by exact operation readback, and prove one POST; action reconciliation returns revision 2 with no stale Waiting for review surface, while Today suppresses the duplicate row for that same Pursuit.

Deletion preserves the recruiter-confirmed value and receipt while degrading evidence authority, redacts source-derived Proposal narrative and decided values, removes the deletion canary from API and operational stores, revokes access, and treats retry idempotently.

Same-name People remain separate IDs, ambiguous capture enters mandatory identity review, the iOS receipt exposes Person/role/context identifiers, and name alone never supplies automatic bind or merge authority.

Generated Agent content remains proposal-only: 30 deterministic trials show a four-tool allowlist, zero external effects, review-only Proposals, quarantine for injection/malformed/stale-source paths, and no authority to mutate confirmed state.
missing_evidence: Complete manual VoiceOver traversal by a human remains unperformed.
Physical-device Action Button, microphone, and system-capture privacy behavior remain unverified.
Five credentialed live Claude Agent SDK trials against a pinned model remain missing; the frozen live artifact truthfully records not_run_missing_credentials.
Production authentication, retention/deletion operations, backup/vendor handling, regional controls, provider reconciliation, and cross-tenant adversarial testing remain unproven.
Design-partner recruiter field comparison and authorized candidate-side experience outcomes remain unmeasured.
open_questions: Should multiple concurrent owned-action recovery operations be a supported V1 state for a recruiter managing several live Pursuits, and if so what is the bounded Today disclosure contract?
Are conflict and failed Proposal rows intentionally historical-only, or are they meant to remain actionable members of the canonical open-Proposal queue after a later Pursuit revision?

reviews.lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: The frozen small-device run directly proves the 375x667 AX5 dark, Reduce Motion Proposal-to-owned-action journey is reachable and passes 3/3 tests, but it does not include a human VoiceOver traversal or physical-device input proof.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-04; evidence/ios-375x667-runtime.json reports iPhone SE (3rd generation), 375x667, iOS 26.5, accessibility-extra-extra-extra-large, dark, 3 passed and 0 failed; /tmp/talent-signal-se-375x667-retest-04-final.xcresult records testCanonicalWorkspaceAX5DarkReducedMotionKeepsNavigationReachable(), testCaptureRailOpensPurposeBoundChooserBeforeAnyCapture(), and testAudioSignalAX5DarkKeepsConsentAndStopReachable() as Passed; evidence/screenshots/se-375x667-ax5-today.png, se-375x667-proposal-receipt.png, se-375x667-action-outcome.png, se-375x667-capture-chooser.png, and se-375x667-audio-saved.png are visually legible. The runtime artifact itself states that manual VoiceOver remains separate human evidence.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter using VoiceOver could still encounter an incorrect reading order, duplicate speech, or a focus trap that visual screenshots and programmatic tapping do not expose.
findings.recommendation: Run the full critical path with a human VoiceOver user on the small and large supported iPhone, including Capture, exact evidence, Proposal decisions, confirmation, canonical receipt, owned action outcome, response loss, and restored evidence review.
findings.verification: Retain a screen recording and accessibility transcript showing identity and exact evidence announced before each consequential control, no focus trap or duplicate speech, and every primary, dismiss, edit, recovery, and audit control reachable in logical order.

findings.observation: The failed-superseded-save/relaunch guard is executable and fail-closed, and the UI source selects the truthful 'Check current evidence' action for a restored operation, but the frozen bundle has no integrated UI test or screenshot that launches that persisted state and observes the displayed affordance before any retry.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-04; /tmp/talent-signal-full-retest-04-final-02.xcresult records RelationshipArchiveTests/testSupersededPersistenceFailureKeepsSessionTerminalGuard(), testRestoredEvidenceReviewUnlocksOnlyAfterExactAuthorityReadback(), and testRestoredEvidenceReviewBecomesTerminalAfterNewerAuthorityReadback() as Passed; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveModels.swift restores pending/outcomeUnknown/failed operations into evidenceReviewAuthorityReadbackKeys and prevents claimEvidenceReview; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAskView.swift renders 'Check current evidence' instead of 'Reconcile safely' when that key is present. None of the 21 frozen screenshots captures this restored card state.
findings.user_impact: The no-POST authority guard is directly supported, so this is not an active duplicate-write veto; however, the exact recruiter-facing recovery wording and affordance after relaunch remain supported inference rather than observed UI behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add a launch-level UI fixture for the failed local superseded-state save, terminate and relaunch, and assert the restored card exposes only 'Check current evidence' before an explicit Ask.
findings.verification: The UI test must assert the obsolete reconcile control is absent, 'Check current evidence' is visible and hittable, the evidence-review POST count stays unchanged before explicit Ask, exact canonical readback unlocks the same operation, and newer authority produces a terminal superseded state.

findings.observation: At 375x667 AX5 dark, the Today screenshot keeps the Person, Pursuit, due context, target, blocker, owner, and provenance readable, but the fixed Ask bar occupies the bottom of the first viewport and the focus card's primary action begins below it, so the action requires scrolling before it is understandable.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-04; evidence/screenshots/se-375x667-ax5-today.png shows the focus card continuing beneath the fixed Ask bar; testCanonicalWorkspaceAX5DarkReducedMotionKeepsNavigationReachable() still passes by scrolling to and activating the Proposal and owned-action controls, so reachability is direct and clipping is not established.
findings.user_impact: A time-constrained recruiter at maximum Dynamic Type may need an extra exploratory scroll before discovering the dominant decision, slightly weakening first-viewport action clarity without blocking completion.
findings.recommendation: At accessibility sizes, reduce the persistent Ask bar footprint or add an explicit continuation cue while preserving the safe-area inset and 44-point targets.
findings.verification: On a 375x667 AX5 dark build, a first-use recruiter identifies the primary action without guessing, and the full action remains reachable with no content obscured at the end of the scroll.

strengths: The 375x667 AX5 dark, Reduce Motion critical Proposal-to-action loop is direct Simulator evidence: all three selected tests pass, Proposal confirmation records revision 1 to 2, and the owned outcome records canonical revision 2 to 3 without exposing an external write.

Response-loss feedback is calm and truthful: the locked screen says the outcome is unknown, the relaunch recovery card replaces the same Pursuit's ordinary attention row, and the reconciled detail shows ACTIVE · REVISION 2 with no stale 'Waiting for review' text or Proposal control; the test also verifies exactly one action POST.

The capture chooser states purpose before capture and explicitly says that capture confirms neither identity, facts, nor an external write; the audio surface keeps purpose, authorizing party, basis, attestation, local-only receipt, and deletion control readable at AX5 dark.

Across the frozen light and dark screenshots, scarce vermilion, strong typography, plain-language receipts, nearby provenance, and restrained cards create a distinctive but quiet hierarchy rather than AI theater.

reviews.lens: human connection, trust, agency, communication, collaboration

findings.observation: While an owned-action response is still unknown, the locked Pursuit screen continues to present the older base-revision Proposal under ‘Waiting for review’. Canonical readback later removes it, but the interim screen leaves two incompatible pieces of work competing for the recruiter's attention.
findings.evidence: [direct] Frozen screenshot evidence/screenshots/action-response-loss-locked.png shows ‘Outcome unknown — operation locked’ and a base-revision-1 Proposal under ‘Waiting for review’ on the same Pursuit. apps/ios/UITests/CandidateSignalUITests.swift testOwnedActionResponseLossRelaunchReconcilesWithoutSecondPost then proves one action POST, a deduplicated Today recovery entry, ACTIVE REVISION 2, and no ‘Waiting for review’ or Proposal control after readback; evidence/pursuit-domain/pursuit-domain-runtime.json records action_revision_supersedes_open_proposal=pass.
findings.user_impact: The backend guard prevents a stale canonical write and no candidate-facing effect exists, so this is not an active harm gate. However, a recruiter can spend attention opening work that may already be obsolete, delaying clear follow-through in a candidate-sensitive moment.
findings.recommendation: When a Pursuit has unresolved action recovery, replace every revision-changing Proposal control with one candid ‘Check current state first’ notice until canonical readback completes.
findings.verification: Extend the response-loss UI test to assert that the locked pre-readback screen exposes no actionable Proposal button, then retain the existing assertions that reconciliation performs no second POST and canonical revision 2 contains no stale Proposal.

findings.observation: The audio flow records an authorizing-party label, an authorization-basis label, and a recruiter attestation, but this frozen local artifact does not prove that the candidate understood the purpose, controlled the choice, or could exercise withdrawal on their own terms.
findings.evidence: [supported inference] Frozen screenshot evidence/screenshots/audio-authorization-receipt.png directly shows purpose-bound fields, a recruiter attestation, protected local storage, no upload, and ‘Revoke authorization and delete recording’. artifact.json also explicitly lists physical-device microphone behavior and authorized candidate-side field outcomes as missing proof; no real candidate data was used.
findings.user_impact: The current safeguards make covert or accidental capture harder and keep this synthetic build non-consequential, but recruiter-entered consent metadata must not later be treated as proof of candidate comprehension or ongoing permission.
findings.recommendation: Before any real-candidate rollout, pair recruiter attestation with a candidate-readable purpose, retention, sharing, and withdrawal explanation, then validate comprehension and withdrawal behavior with authorized participants. Preserve uncertainty when consent proof is absent.
findings.verification: On a physical device, run authorized participant sessions covering permission refusal, recording interruption, revocation, deletion, and re-capture. Pass only if no audio starts before permission, revoked audio and derivatives become unavailable, and participants can accurately explain purpose, retention, and withdrawal.

strengths: Restored evidence-review work fails closed: apps/ios/Tests/RelationshipArchiveTests.swift proves a failed superseded-state save remains readback-locked after relaunch, an exact current citation unlocks, and newer authority terminally supersedes the older operation.

Identity handling protects the person behind the record: the same-name UI journey searches by stable identity clues, preserves the selected Person/Pursuit across relaunch, and reads exact Person, role, context, Capture, and Resource identifiers back before claiming success.

Deletion is candid and operationally sequenced. The UI says server deletion was confirmed before the local payload was removed, while pursuit-evidence-integrity-runtime.json proves source-derived narrative redaction, unavailable authority, deletion-canary absence, and idempotent retry.

Response-loss recovery reduces misoperation: the owned-action test proves one POST, one recovery entry instead of duplicate Today attention, canonical receipt readback, and removal of the stale Proposal after the revision advances.

Generated content stays advisory and internal. The deterministic Agent artifact reports 30 passing trials, a four-tool read/stage-only manifest, review-only Proposals, and zero external effects; P0-07 likewise keeps owned actions free of messages, meetings, notifications, or external writes.

The UI uses candid uncertainty rather than faux empathy or pressure: saved responses mark stale citations, unknown outcomes lock operations, reviewed evidence remains distinguishable from inference, and silence is not converted into a candidate score or rejection signal.
missing_evidence: Complete manual VoiceOver traversal by a human across the critical candidate-sensitive journey.
Physical-device Action Button, microphone, and system-capture privacy behavior, including permission denial, interruption, and revocation.
Five credentialed live Claude Agent SDK trials against the frozen evaluator; the frozen live-provider artifact correctly remains missing proof.
Production authentication, retention/deletion operations, regional controls, provider reconciliation, and cross-tenant adversarial testing.

Authorized recruiter and candidate field outcomes showing that the workflow improves listening, timely follow-through, correction, consent comprehension, and humane closure without increasing interruption.
open_questions: What candidate-visible or candidate-verifiable record will distinguish actual permission from a recruiter-entered consent assertion when real audio capture is introduced?
How will the internal owned-action receipt translate into timely human follow-through without introducing automated pressure or candidate-facing ghosting?

top_findings.reason: Today projects only the newest owned-action recovery, so an older safe-but-unresolved recovery can lose its Today entry when several Pursuits suffer response loss.
top_findings.next_step: Project a compact recovery entry for every affected Pursuit and deduplicate the ordinary attention row for each exact recovery Pursuit.
top_findings.verification: Two response-lost Pursuits both remain reachable after relaunch, neither is duplicated, each readback binds its own operation and receipt, and each POST count remains exactly one.

top_findings.reason: Before an unknown owned-action outcome is reconciled, the same Pursuit can still show its older Proposal as waiting for review even though the canonical revision may already have advanced.
top_findings.next_step: Replace revision-changing Proposal controls with a truthful current-state check while any owned-action recovery for that Pursuit is unresolved.
top_findings.verification: The locked pre-readback screen has no actionable Proposal control; reconciliation still performs no second POST and the canonical revision contains no stale open Proposal.

top_findings.reason: Automated 375x667 AX5 dark coverage is direct, but manual VoiceOver, physical-device capture and microphone behavior, credentialed Claude, production controls, and real recruiter/candidate outcomes remain unobserved.
top_findings.next_step: Run the authorized physical accessibility, production-safety, credentialed-provider, and design-partner field matrix without introducing real candidate data into synthetic fixtures.
top_findings.verification: Critical journeys remain understandable, reachable, nonduplicative, reversible, consent-aware, and evidence-bound under real assistive, device, provider, and field conditions.

agreements: All four reviewers independently verified the same 195 source, 39 runtime-evidence, and 21 screenshot hashes, the aggregate source digest, and frozen commit.
No reviewer issued an active veto; every specialist scored the scoped local V1 at 3/4, and scores remain attached to their own rubrics rather than averaged.

Restored evidence-review operations fail closed across failed terminal persistence and relaunch, require an explicit Ask plus exact current canonical authority readback, and terminally supersede on newer authority.
Proposal and owned-action response loss withhold success, preserve one operation identity, reconcile by exact canonical readback, and prove one POST with no external effect.

Action revision canonically supersedes the tested older needs-review Proposal and the reconciled iOS surface removes stale review authority; Today suppresses duplicate attention for that recovery Pursuit.
Same-name identity, deletion redaction, temporal authority, human review, and proposal-only Agent boundaries remain directly evidenced.
Manual accessibility, physical device, credentialed live provider, production/cross-tenant, and field outcomes remain missing proof and cannot be converted into release claims.
adjudication.rationale: The frozen repository V1 integration gate passes: deterministic experience is 99/100, review/documentation is 100/100, critical failures are zero, all twelve P0 journeys pass, the full and smallest-device iOS gates pass, repository checks pass, and four independent specialists report no active veto. The release gate applies only to merging this scoped synthetic/local V1 implementation. It does not claim production readiness, candidate consent effectiveness, physical-device accessibility, credentialed Claude reliability, or field impact. The remaining findings are bounded follow-up work because current guards prevent duplicate writes, stale canonical mutation, external effects, candidate ranking, and false success.
